messages:
Ibrahim: Weird morning 10am call dropped twice, lights dimmed for a second and internet hiccuped. Neighbor just installed an EV charger yesterday. Anyone seen chargers cause home network weirdness? :electric_plug:

Priya: That can happen if the building wiring sags when the charger kicks in. Powerline adapters especially hate that. Any packet loss or jitter when it happens?

Ibrahim: Yep, ran a ping while it happened and saw big spikes:

Ibrahim: ```
$ ping -c 6 8.8.8.8
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=18.6 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=117 time=457.3 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=117 time=19.2 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=4 ttl=117 time=16.8 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=5 ttl=117 time=512.9 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=6 ttl=117 time=18.0 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
6 packets transmitted, 6 received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 16.8/173.8/512.9 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed ibrahim-laptop power-sag correlated spike at 2425000104; peak RTT 513ms, 3 retransmits in 20m window. Recommendation: avoid powerline adapters during charger test, consider UPS for modem+router.

Nora: If the building's neutral is shared, EV chargers can cause voltage dips. Landlord/HOA needs to check panel capacity. Meanwhile, try tethering or a small UPS for the router/modem.

Ken: Temporary hack: plug router and modem into a UPS (even a small one) so brief sags don't reboot network gear. Also check router logs for WAN flaps.

Ibrahim: I don't have a UPS yet. Quick test 1 unplugged powerline adapter and moved laptop to 5GHz; ran ping again during neighbor charging and it's smoother:

Ibrahim: ```
$ ping -c 6 8.8.8.8
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=17.9 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=117 time=18.4 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=117 time=16.5 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=4 ttl=117 time=17.2 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=5 ttl=117 time=17.0 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=6 ttl=117 time=16.8 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
6 packets transmitted, 6 received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 16.5/17.3/18.4 ms
```

Priya: Nice repro. That makes powerline the likely culprit. Powerline adapters ride the mains; any voltage instability equals noisy packets. UPS for modem/router or wiring check with landlord is the right next step.

Ibrahim: Filed a note with building mgmt. Ordered a small UPS. Poll: react with :battery: if you think UPS is the way, :truck: if you think I should demand the neighbor move the charger install, :phone: for "tether and survive". GIFs welcome.

Ken: UPS + polite building escalations. And a funny router name: "ChargeDrop" or "EV-erlastingConnect". Vote or add puns.

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: monitoring ibrahim-laptop for further transients; alert threshold set at RTT >300ms.

Ibrahim: Thanks y'all 1 will report back after UPS arrives and after building gets their electrician to sanity-check panels. Photo of the charging station outside for context: https://images.redwood.example/ev-charger-building.jpg :oncoming_automobile:
